 All agenda items and reports are available for review in the City Clerk’s Office and
 www.hpca.gov. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding
 any item on this agenda (other than writings legally exempt from public disclosure) will be
 made available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk located at 6550 Miles
 Avenue, Huntington Park, California 90255 during regular business hours, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30
 p.m., Monday – Thursday, and at the City Hall Council Chambers during the meeting.

 Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, including
 auxiliary aids or services, in order to participate in the public meeting may request such
 modification, accommodation, aid or service by contacting the City Clerk’s Office either in
 person at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California or by telephone at (323) 584-6230.
 Notification in advance of the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements
 to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

 PLEASE SILENCE ALL CELL PHONES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC
 EQUIPMENT WHILE COUNCIL IS IN SESSION. Thank you.

PLEASE NOTE-The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
  May 26, 2026  Page 1 of 6
  decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
 are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
 the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code, commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each
  speaker will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed
  on the City Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the
  City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct
  disruptive to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of
  Procedure or conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council
  Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must
  be directed to the mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

 We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required
 for the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

For both open and closed sessions, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
public hearing items.

All comments or queries should be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.

minutes_text:
Tuesday Meeting of the
  City of Huntington Park City Council
  Tuesday, May 26, 2026

 The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
 called to order at 6:06 p.m. on Tuesday, May 26, 2026, in the Council Chambers at City
 Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Eduardo “Eddie” Martinez
 presiding.

 PRESENT: Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria, and Mayor
 Martinez

 ABSENT: Council Member(s): Flores

 CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: Eduardo Sarmiento City Clerk; Louis Morales Interim
 Community Development Director; Cosme Lozano Chief of Police; Jeff Jones Finance
 Director, Gerardo “Gerry” Lopez Public Works Director; Cynthia Norzagaray Parks and Recreation
 Director; Andrew Sarega City Attorney; Stephany Santin Assistant City Manager; and
 Ricardo Reyes City Manager.

INVOCATION
 Invocation led by Mayor Martinez

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
 Pledge of Allegiance led by Vice Mayor Sanabria.

PRESENTATION(S)

 1.  SOUTHEAST LOS ANGELESS OPEN STREETS EVENT 2026

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

  1. Eddie Benitez- Concerns about Tree Shavings near his house.
  2. Victor Ramirez
  3. Rudy Cruz- Cost for the Art Walk.
  4. John Doe- Parking is bad, asking for update on Measure PP.
  5. Ms. Cobarubias- Rental assistant program is not responding.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
CITY CLERK

1.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:
  Approve Minute(s) of the following City Council Meeting(s):
  1. Study Session Meeting April 28, 2026
  2. Regular City Council Meeting May 12, 2026
FINANCE

2.  WARRANT REGISTERS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve Accounts Payable and Payroll Warrant(s) dated May 19, 2026

HUMAN RESOURCES

3.  AUTHORIZE AND APPROVE CORRECTED EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT FOR
  HUMAN RESOURCES DIRECTOR WITH ANA KARINA RUEDA

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:
   1. Approve a corrected employment agreement with Ana Karina Rueda, Human
  Resources Director, correcting the annual salary amount from $161,733 to
  $173,024; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the employment agreement in a form
  approved by the City Attorney; and
  3. Direct staff to make any necessary personnel and payroll record adjustments
  consistent with the corrected agreement.

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to approve the consent calendar in
  its entirety. The motion was seconded by Councilmember Martiz.
  Councilmember Macias abstained from voting on the motion.
  Councilmember Flores was absent. The motion was carried by
  majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s) Martiz, Vice Mayor Sanabria and Mayor
  Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): Macias

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

  END OF CONSENT CALENDAR

  PUBLIC HEARING(S)

  NONE

  END OF PUBLIC HEARINGS

  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

FINANCE

1.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO PROVIDE DIRECTION, TAKE PUBLIC
  INPUT, AND DIRECT THE CITY MANAGER AND FINANCE DIRECTOR TO MAKE
  FINAL CHANGES TO THE PROPOSED BUDGET FOR THE FISCAL YEAR
  BEGINNING JULY 1, 2026, AND ENDING JUNE 30, 2027

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Review and Present the Draft FY 2026 – 2027 Proposed Budget; and

  2. Direct the City Manager and Director of Finance to make any final revisions to the
  Proposed Budget, as necessary. If no revisions are required, consider and approve
  the resolutions adopting the City of Huntington Park’s Fiscal Year 2026–27
  Operating Budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, and ending June 30,
  2027; and

  3. Adopt a Resolution adopting a Budget for the Fiscal Year Commencing July 1,
  2026, and ending June 30, 2027, Making Appropriations for the Conduct of City of
  Huntington Park Government, Establishing Policies for the Administration of the
  Adopted Budget, and for other Budget Related Purposes; and

  4. Adopt a Resolution Establishing the GANN appropriation limit pursuant to the
  provisions of the California Constitution Article XIIIB for the Fiscal Year Beginning
  July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2027.

  MOTION: Councilmember Martiz stated how the parking program will require robust
  program with a multi prolonged approach. She also stated how the skate park
  concept should be part of future budgeting conversation. Councilmember Macias
  asked for a status on the parking permit program. Community Development Director
   Louis Morales said he needs to investigate how much money will be needed.
  Councilmember Macias also asked if there will be more funds to go into the “HP with
  You” program. Councilmember Macias also requested an update on the Water Wells
  presentation. Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to Review and Present the Draft FY
  2026 – 2027 Proposed Budget; and Direct the City Manager and Director of Finance
  to make any final revisions to the Proposed Budget, as necessary. The motion was
  seconded by Councilmember Martiz. Councilmember Flores was absent. The motion
  was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

PUBLIC WORKS

2.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL TO ADOPT THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  BUS SHELTER STANDARD AS CITY OF HUNTINGTON PARK BUS SHELTER
  STANDARD

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Adopt a resolution adopting the County of Los Angeles Bus Shelter Standard as
  City of Huntington Park Bus Shelter Standard.

  MOTION: Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to adopt a resolution adopting the County
  of Los Angeles Bus Shelter Standard as City of Huntington Park Bus Shelter
  Standard. The motion was seconded by Councilmember Martiz. Councilmember
  Macias voted against the motion stating her concerns regarding the design.
  Councilmember Flores was absent. The motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Vice Mayor Sanabria and Mayor
  Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): Macias

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

  REPORTS AND INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

PARKS AND RECREATION

1.  APPROVE RENEWAL OF LICENSE AGREEMENT WITH HARBOR AREA
  FARMERS MARKETS FOR USAGE OF SALT LAKE PARK FROM 2026 - 2029

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve renewal of license agreement with Harbor Area Farmers Markets for
  usage of Salt Lake Park from 2026 – 2029 at the continued payment rate of 1%
  of total farmers market income, with the option to revisit fees; and

  2. Authorize City Manager to execute Agreement.
  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to approve renewal of the license
  agreement with Harbor Area Farmers Markets for usage of Salt Lake Park from 2026
  – 2029 at the continued payment rate of 1% of total farmers market income, with the
  option to revisit fees; and Authorize City Manager to execute Agreement.
   Councilmember Martiz seconded the motion. The motion was carried by majority
  vote.
  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

CITY CLERK

3.  NOMINATION AND CONSIDERATION OF APPOINTMENT TO VARIOUS
  COMMISSIONS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Consideration, nomination and appointment of Commissioner to fill vacancies in
  various commissions.

  MOTION: None. Councilmember Martiz asked if we could include dates and times in
  the future. As well as sharing application via emails. Then, Log who has been
  contacted.

  END OF REPORTS AND INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

  DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

Finance: Take the opportunity to thank his staff and directors for assistance with the
preparation of the Budget.

City Manager: Due to new legal mandates. He read out the Employment agreement for
Ana Karina Ruedas who will serve as the Human Resources Director and her salary
adjustment from 161,733 to 173,024 annual salary.

City Attorney: No Report.

Police: No Report.

Parks and Recreation: Thank Council and Directors for participating in the Memorial
Event. The department will be opening the link for register in the 5K soon.

Community Development: No Report.

Public Works: Thank you to the public who attended the “Touch a Truck” event last
Wednesday. It was a great event.

City Clerk: Primary elections will be held on Tuesday, June 2nd, 2026. Drop Box is
available at the New Start building on Gage Ave. The City Clerk’s page on the website
also has tools to find the nearby Vote Center County wise.

Communication: Police Department with be hosting their “Coffee with a Cop” on June 4th
from 6pm-8pm at Starbucks on Florence. They will also be hosting another “Coffee with a
Cop” on June 25th at the Target. Torch Run will be taking place on Tuesday, June 2 nd
around 2pm. Participants will be receiving it from Bell PD around 2:30pm. Thank you to
everyone who participated at the Art Walk.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
 COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Councilmember Macias: Thank you everyone! Have a good night.

Councilmember Martiz: Wants staff to give us an update on the library. Many residence
believe that it is a City of Huntington Park project; however, it is a county project.

Vice Mayor Sanabria: Thank you to staff for all the work that they did on the budget.
Thank you so much for staff for the work that has been done at the various events. The
artists from Rosarito were very cool. Maybe we could attend one of Rosarito’s events
one day. Memorial Day Service event was great. “Touch a Truck” event was great. He
mentioned how his son was recruiting kids from the playground to blow the horn on one
of the vehicles. Vice Mayor asked questions regarding the PD fundraising event at the
“Carniceria” near Salt Lake Park. Thank you all so much for the work you all do.

Mayor Martinez: Thank you to staff for making sure we’re here safe. Thank you to
everyone who supported and attended the Art Walk. The event is growing and people
like it. Mayor Martinez had the opportunity to attend the Gateway COG and advocate for
the South East Light Rail line. We have an administration that has placed a lot of
projects on hold. He mentioned how the cities of Artesia, Cerritos, and Downey make it a
habit to meet with their representatives, and this leads to potential securing in funding
and wanted to see how Huntington Park could do something similar with our federal,
state, and county representatives. The City Manager, Mayor, and Vice Mayor should
make it a habit to visit them on an annual basis.

  CLOSED SESSION

PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE
Government Code § 54957(b)(1)
Various Matters

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

City Council met in Closed Session to discuss employee discipline matters. No reportable
action was taken.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION: Mayor Martinez adjourned at 8:49pm. The next regular city council meeting is
set to be held on Tuesday, June 9th, 2026 @6pm.

Respectfully submitted,

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
